sections.section_title: Pathophysiology and Clinical Spectrum of Dermatomyositis
sections.description: This section provides the foundational knowledge of dermatomyositis (DM), focusing on its systemic nature, classic cutaneous manifestations, and the specific characteristics of SAE1-positive variants.
subtopics: Definition and epidemiology of idiopathic inflammatory myopathies
Pathogenesis of dermatomyositis: Immune-mediated muscle and skin inflammation
Classic cutaneous markers: Gottron’s papules, heliotrope eruption, and shawl sign
Systemic involvement: Interstitial lung disease, dysphagia, and cardiac considerations
Anti-SAE1 antibodies: Clinical associations with dysphagia, pulmonary involvement, and malignancy risk

sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and the Diagnostic Challenge of Pseudoangioedema
sections.description: This section analyzes the patient's initial presentation, exploring why dermatomyositis can masquerade as other conditions, specifically focusing on the confusion between myositis-related swelling and true angioedema.
subtopics: Initial presentation: Neck swelling, proximal muscle weakness, and myalgia
Differential diagnosis in the emergency setting: Ludwig’s angina vs. deep neck space infections
Distinguishing idiopathic angioedema (histaminergic/bradykinin-mediated) from 'pseudoangioedema'
Subtle physical exam findings: Nailfold capillaroscopy, periungual erythema, and subtle rashes
Clinical reasoning: Why the absence of traditional angioedema triggers (medications, complement levels) should prompt further investigation

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Workup and Evidence for Myositis
sections.description: This section details the transition from an otolaryngology/immunology workup for angioedema to a definitive rheumatological diagnosis using laboratory, imaging, and histological evidence.
subtopics: Initial 'negative' workup for angioedema: C3, C4, and C1 esterase function
Key laboratory pivots: Significant elevation of Creatine Kinase (CK) and transaminases
Serological profiling: ANA titers and the Myositis Antibody Panel (SAE1 positivity)
Advanced imaging: MRI and FDG-PET for identifying active muscle inflammation
Gold standard diagnosis: Muscle biopsy findings (necrotic fibers, perifascicular capillary involvement, and C5b-9 deposition)

sections.description: This section covers the multi-modal treatment approach for severe inflammatory myopathy, the management of complications like dysphagia and aspiration, and the critical importance of malignancy screening.
subtopics: Acute management: High-dose pulse methylprednisolone and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG)
Steroid-sparing agents: Mycophenolate mofetil vs. Methotrexate in the context of lung involvement
Management of complications: Dysphagia, nasogastric tube requirements, and aspiration pneumonitis
Malignancy screening protocols: IMACS guidelines and risk stratification for adult dermatomyositis
Monitoring and outcome: Recovery of muscle strength and resolution of soft tissue swelling
